In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an accelerator for heavy ions which will provide energies up 100 MeV/nucleon and which will have a high duty cycle, high beam quality, high reliability, and a high degree of flexibility for a wide range of experimental applications.
the design and construction of an accelerator system which will provide high energy heavy ions to a wide variety of research programs.
the design and development of the separated-sector cyclotron as a heavy ion accelerator for the Holified Heavy Ion Research Facility.

the Phase II cyclotron will be a very valuable addition to the Phase I HHIRF facility and will provide a very useful and important tool for research in nuclear science and technology.

the design of the HHIRFS separated-sector cyclotron is well advanced and that a design is now available which is technically feasible and which will provide a high quality heavy ion beam at the desired energy levels.

we have a well-defined, well-understood, and relatively simple design for the new separated-sector accelerator.
the Phase I facility will provide a wide variety of ion species and energy combinations for nuclear structure studies and for nuclear reaction studies in general.

the separated-sector cyclotron is a very attractive machine for a wide range of nuclear physics experiments, and the design work for the HHIRF cyclotron is proceeding satisfactorily. 3 figures, 1 table.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to build a cyclotron booster accelerator with a large energy range and with a high efficiency for heavy ion beams, and with a high reliability.
the design of a cyclotron for the purpose of boosting tandem beams requires special attention to be given to beam optics and beam dynamics.
a separated-sector cyclotron is an attractive alternative to the isochronous design, particularly when high energies are desired.
